meaning:
1) plowman, husbandman, farmer
1a) working the land, yet not owning any of it

elsewhere.note: He built towers in the wilderness, and dug out many cisterns, for he had much livestock; in the lowland also, and in the plain. He had farmers and vineyard…
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks. Foreigners will work your fields and your vineyards.
Because of the ground which is cracked, because no rain has been in the land, the plowmen are disappointed. They cover their heads.
Be confounded, you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers; for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field has perished.
